title: Cryo-ADF-STEM Imaging of Crown Ether-Based Polyamide Membrane
content: Separation membranes play a critical role in a number of energy applications, from batteries to desalination. Additionally, such membranes can be used to capture valuable ionic species, such as lithium, for the manufacture of state-of-the-art energy storage devices. Crown ethers in particular are well-known for their ability to selectively capture alkali metal ions, making them ideal candidates for separation membranes [1]. Characterization of these membranes is critical to inform renewed synthesis efforts. While atomic resolution images of crown ethers in graphene have been achieved by medium-angle annular dark field (ADF) STEM imaging [2], polymeric crown ether-based membranes remain challenging to characterize with S/TEM, due to their beam sensitive nature.
